learning.title: A heartbeat body restored from a killed worker never renames the restarted process
learning.trigger: A worker is killed after it saved a pending heartbeat body and before the server committed it, then restarts from the same state directory.
learning.mistake: The restarted process sent the restored body first. The server never committed that key, accepted the body from the host's current session and answered that session as a new one, and runHeartbeatLoop took the answer as the process session. The worker claimed under the killed worker's session and its new attempt kept it (main push run 41401773074; 1 of 12 runs on main).
learning.rule: In runHeartbeatLoop a response to a body whose workerSessionId differs from state.processSessionId is handled as a replay: no rename, no ready signal, an immediate takeover heartbeat. Do not drop the restored body at startup: a committed-but-unacknowledged first heartbeat would then be fenced.

verification.requirement: tests/helpers/worker-execution/recovery-locks.ts restart sends an uncommitted heartbeat first without adopting its process session fails at 6097629f and passes after the fix.

Injecting a never-sent pending body into the killed worker's registration.json makes the fixed-coding-preset recovery child fail at the base with the same session id on both sides, and pass with the fix.
